title.narrative: Provision of equitable access to quality life-saving primary health care services for vulnerable drought and conflict affected communities in Afgooye

description.narrative:
ltp class="MsoNormal" style="mso-margin-top-alt:automso-margin-bottom-alt:auto text-align:justifyline-height:normal"gtltspan style="font-size: 14px"gtAccording to the (FSNAU) reports, approximately 8.3 million people across Somalia are expected to face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity outcomes between April and June 2023. This unprecedented level of need within Somalia is driven by the impacts of five consecutive seasons of poor rainfall, a likely sixth season of below-average rainfall from March to June 2023, and exceptionally high food prices, exacerbated by concurrent conflict/insecurity and disease outbreaks. Afgoie corridor hosts IDPs migrated from neighboring districts and regions most of them have been stayed there for a long, while other new IDP families arrived due to the current drought in the country. Measles, AWD/cholera are among the common diseases suffered by the IDP communities. The proposed project aims to cover the health needs of drought and conflict-affected IDP communities particularly women, including pregnant and lactating, men, boys, girls, and people with disabilities (PWDs) at risk of famine. The project will aim at providing curative and preventive, basic lifesaving health services among the communities of the target locations in Afgoie corridor through establishment of 2 health fixed sites and 2 mobile teams for outreach services. An estimated beneficiary of 33,000 persons, including 4,500 Men, 14,500 women, 6,500 boys, and 7,500 girls will be reached by the project for alt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 14px" lang="EN-GB"gt period of 12 months.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgt
